internal_existence_statements_not_export.name: NavierStokes.ProblemStatement primitives
internal_existence_statements_not_export.text:
abbrev Space := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)  -- 30
abbrev SpaceTime := ℝ × Space  -- 33 (time first)
abbrev VelocityField := SpaceTime → Space  -- 35
abbrev PressureField := SpaceTime → ℝ  -- 36
def coordinateVector (i : Fin 3) : Space := EuclideanSpace.single i 1  -- 39
def preSingularDomain : Set SpaceTime := Ico 0 1 ×ˢ univ  -- 42
def futureDomain : Set SpaceTime := Ici 0 ×ˢ univ  -- 45
def UnitSpatialPeriodsOn {V : Type*} (times : Set ℝ) (g : SpaceTime → V) : Prop :=
  ∀ t ∈ times, ∀ x : Space, ∀ i : Fin 3,
    g (t, x + coordinateVector i) = g (t, x)  -- 49
def temporalDerivative (u : VelocityField) (t : ℝ) (x : Space) : Space :=
  fderiv ℝ (fun s : ℝ => u (s, x)) t 1  -- 55
def spatialDerivative (u : VelocityField) (t : ℝ) (x : Space) : Space →L[ℝ] Space :=
  fderiv ℝ (fun y : Space => u (t, y)) x  -- 59
def advection (u : VelocityField) (t : ℝ) (x : Space) : Space :=
  spatialDerivative u t x (u (t, x))  -- 63
def spatialDivergence (u : VelocityField) (t : ℝ) (x : Space) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i : Fin 3, (spatialDerivative u t x (coordinateVector i)) i  -- 67
def pressureGradient (p : PressureField) (t : ℝ) (x : Space) : Space :=
  ∑ i : Fin 3,
    (fderiv ℝ (fun y : Space => p (t, y)) x (coordinateVector i)) • coordinateVector i  -- 71
def spatialLaplacian (u : VelocityField) (t : ℝ) (x : Space) : Space :=
  ∑ i : Fin 3,
    fderiv ℝ (fun y : Space => spatialDerivative u t y (coordinateVector i))
      x (coordinateVector i)  -- 76
def navierStokesResidual (u : VelocityField) (p : PressureField)
    (t : ℝ) (x : Space) : Space :=
  temporalDerivative u t x + advection u t x - spatialLaplacian u t x +
    pressureGradient p t x  -- 82 (viscosity exactly one)
def CompactFutureTimeSupport (f : VelocityField) : Prop :=
  ∃ T : ℝ, 0 ≤ T ∧ ∀ t : ℝ, T ≤ t → ∀ x : Space, f (t, x) = 0  -- 89
def SpeedUnboundedAtOne (u : VelocityField) : Prop :=
  ∀ M : ℝ, 0 < M → ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ →
    ∃ t : ℝ, ∃ x : Space, t ∈ Ioo 0 1 ∧ 1 - δ < t ∧ M < ‖u (t, x)‖  -- 94
internal_existence_statements_not_export.role: Primitives of the project's own (non-comparator) statements.

def breakdownStatement : Prop :=
  ∀ ν : ℝ, 0 < ν →
    ∃ u : VelocityField, ∃ p : PressureField, ∃ f : VelocityField, ∃ K : Set Space,
      CandidateProperties ν u p f K ∧ ¬ Nonempty (GlobalFiniteEnergySolution ν f)
-- with (line 92) structure CandidateProperties (ν : ℝ) (u : VelocityField) (p : PressureField)
    (f : VelocityField) (K : Set Space) : Prop where
  velocity_smooth : ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ u preSingularDomain
  pressure_smooth : ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ p preSingularDomain
  support_compact : IsCompact K
  velocity_support : ∀ t ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) 1,
    tsupport (fun x : Space => u (t, x)) ⊆ K
  pressure_support : ∀ t ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) 1,
    tsupport (fun x : Space => p (t, x)) ⊆ K
  force_smooth : ContDiff ℝ ∞ f
  force_support : CompactPositiveTimeSupport f
  zero_initial_velocity : ∀ x : Space, u (0, x) = 0
  divergence_free : ∀ t ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ x : Space,
    NavierStokes.ProblemStatement.spatialDivergence u t x = 0
  navier_stokes : ∀ t ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ x : Space,
    navierStokesResidual ν u p t x = f (t, x)
  energy_bounded : UniformFiniteEnergy (Ico 0 1) u
  speed_unbounded : SpeedUnboundedAtOne u
-- def CompactPositiveTimeSupport (f) : Prop := HasCompactSupport f ∧ tsupport f ⊆ positiveTimeDomain (line 66; positiveTimeDomain := Ioi 0 ×ˢ univ, line 53)
-- def UniformFiniteEnergy (times) (u) : Prop := ∃ E : ℝ, 0 ≤ E ∧ ∀ t ∈ times, SquareIntegrableAtTime u t ∧ kineticEnergy u t ≤ E (line 81)

reference_texts.theorem_1_1: For every ν > 0 there exist a force f ∈ C∞c (R3 × (0, ∞); R3), a compact set K ⊂ R3, and smooth velocity and pressure fields u, p on R3 × [0, 1) satisfying ∂tu + (u · ∇)u − ν∆u + ∇p = f, ∇· u = 0, u(·, 0) = 0, (1.1) such that supp u(·, t) ∪ supp p(·, t) ⊂ K for every 0 ≤ t < 1, sup_{0≤t<1} ∥u(t)∥L2(R3) < ∞, lim sup_{t↑1} ∥u(t)∥L∞(R3) = ∞. Consequently, there is no smooth solution (u, P) on R3 × [0, ∞) with the same force and initial datum whose kinetic energy is uniformly bounded sup_{t≥0} ½∫ |u(x, t)|² dx < ∞. (manuscript_pages.txt, page 1)
reference_texts.corollary_10_6: For every ν > 0, there is a smooth force on T3 × [0, ∞), compactly supported in time, for which the solution (U, Pper) of the periodic Navier–Stokes equations with viscosity ν and zero initial velocity is smooth on [0, 1) and satisfies lim sup_{t↑1} ∥U(t)∥L∞(T3) = ∞. Its velocity and pressure have support in a fixed compact subset of the interior of Q0 at every time before one. There is no global smooth periodic solution for the same datum and force. (manuscript_pages.txt, page 125)
reference_texts.fefferman_C: (C) Breakdown of Navier–Stokes solutions on R3. Take ν > 0 and n = 3. Then there exist a smooth, divergence-free vector field u◦(x) on R3 and a smooth f(x, t) on R3 × [0, ∞), satisfying (4), (5), for which there exist no solutions (p, u) of (1), (2), (3), (6), (7) on R3 × [0, ∞). [(4) |∂^α_x u◦(x)| ≤ C_{αK}(1+|x|)^{-K}; (5) |∂^α_x ∂^m_t f(x,t)| ≤ C_{αmK}(1+|x|+t)^{-K} on R^n×[0,∞); (6) p,u ∈ C∞(R^n×[0,∞)); (7) ∫_{R^n}|u(x,t)|²dx < C for all t ≥ 0 (bounded energy)] (Clay PDF pages 1-2)
reference_texts.fefferman_D: (D) Breakdown of Navier–Stokes Solutions on R3/Z3. Take ν > 0 and n = 3. Then there exist a smooth, divergence-free vector field u◦(x) on R3 and a smooth f(x, t) on R3 × [0, ∞), satisfying (8), (9), for which there exist no solutions (p, u) of (1), (2), (3), (10), (11) on R3 × [0, ∞). [(8) u◦(x+e_j)=u◦(x), f(x+e_j,t)=f(x,t); (9) |∂^α_x ∂^m_t f| ≤ C_{αmK}(1+|t|)^{-K} on R3×[0,∞); (10) u(x,t)=u(x+e_j,t) on R3×[0,∞); (11) p,u ∈ C∞(R^n×[0,∞)); Errata (PDF page 6): 'The further condition p(x + ej, t) = p(x, t) should be made explicit in Eqn (8).'] (Clay PDF pages 2, 6)

verdict.why: The top-level Lean theorem `NavierStokes.Comparator.navier_stokes_breakdown_R3` is a verbatim transcription of Fefferman's alternative (C) — '∀ν>0 ∃ u₀,f in decay classes (4),(5) with no global smooth bounded-energy solution' — i.e. it formalizes only the paper's one-line 'Consequently' corollary of Theorem 1.1 and none of the displayed statement: it asserts no blowing-up solution, no compact K, no support containment, no bounded energy of the constructed flow, no limsup L∞ = ∞, no fixed singular time t=1, and it quantifies an arbitrary decaying u₀ and a merely polynomially-decaying f rather than u₀=0 and f ∈ C∞_c(R³×(0,∞)); every one of these Lean clauses is implied by Theorem 1.1 (with u₀=0 and the compactly supported f), while the Lean statement does not imply the existence clauses, so it is strictly weaker as a proposition. The only clause-for-clause match of Theorem 1.1 in the repository, `NavierStokesR3.ProblemStatement.breakdownStatement` (R3/ProblemStatement.lean:150), is a definition that no theorem proves; the closest proved existence statement, `R3CompactCandidate.selected_compact_candidate` (viscosity one only), lacks the sup L² < ∞ clause and uses two separate support sets.
